title: Gregg Williams Sweeps Trophy and Jacket
title_candidates: Gregg Williams Sweeps Trophy and Jacket
Williams Seals the Double at Oitavos
The Double Lands at Oitavos Dunes
theme: Composure at the top, carnage everywhere else.
tone: Wry and affectionate; solemn treatment of small triumphs and comic disasters alike.
opening_hook: On the rugged links of Oitavos Dunes, Gregg Williams closed out TEG 15 with the untroubled calm of a man who had already banked the outcome, while behind him the rest of the field conducted a highlights reel of everything that can go wrong in golf.

round_story.subject: Stuart Neumann posts the best Stableford round of the day, then contrives a quintuple bogey at the final hole to spoil it.
round_story.why_it_matters: It was the single best scoring return of the round, a reminder of what Neumann can do on his day, and, in the way of TEG, it still ended in a snowman.
round_story.shape: Neumann strings together the tournament's best final-round points tally, surging up the Trophy table; needing only a tidy finish, he then runs up a nine at the 18th, the sting in the tail of an otherwise flawless card.
headline_candidates: Neumann's Best Round Ends in a Nine
The Best Round, Ruined at the Last
Neumann Peaks, Then Blows Up at 18
round_story.chosen_headline: Neumann's Best Round Ends in a Nine
round_story.standfirst: A career-quality Stableford return took a wrong turn at the very last hole of the week.

race_story.subject: Gregg Williams closes out TEG 15 with victories in both the Trophy and the Green Jacket, completing the tournament's sixth double.
race_story.why_it_matters: It confirms Williams as the dominant force of the week, having led both competitions wire to wire, and marks a rare feat in TEG's own history.
race_story.shape: Arriving with commanding overnight leads in both races, Williams answers with 34 Stableford points and a personal-best 91 gross round at Oitavos Dunes, seeing off Stuart Neumann by 21 in the Trophy and Jon Baker by 29 in the Green Jacket; he becomes only the sixth player to complete the double.
headline_candidates: Gregg Williams Seals Trophy and Jacket
race_story.standfirst: A sixth Trophy-and-Jacket double in TEG history, delivered with the same calm that carried him through all four rounds.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin's final round produces his worst Stableford and worst gross scores in the same afternoon, capped by a quadruple bogey at the last.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It was the worst round of Mullin's 55-round TEG career by both counting methods, coming straight off his best round of the week, and it nearly cost him his escape from the Wooden Spoon.
discovered_storylines.shape: Mullin arrives at Oitavos Dunes fresh from his best round of the tournament, opens with three ropey holes, fades further through the closing stretch, and finishes with a quadruple bogey at the 18th for a career-worst 22 points and +33 gross.
headline_candidates: Mullin Hits Rock Bottom at Oitavos
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Two personal worsts in one afternoon, and a nervous look over the shoulder at the Wooden Spoon.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson opens with a sextuple bogey at the 1st, bleeds ten shots across the first three holes, and never finds a rhythm.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It cost him outright second place in the Trophy race, dropping him from runner-up overnight to third by the close.
discovered_storylines.shape: Patterson's week unravels from the very first tee, a ten at the 1st followed by two more dropped-shot holes leaving him without a net par through three; a brief truce at 15-16 offers false hope before further blow-ups at 12 and 17 confirm the theme.
headline_candidates: Patterson's Ten at the First Sets the Tone
A Sextuple Bogey to Begin the Day
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Patterson's Ten at the First Sets the Tone
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A calamitous start on the very first hole shaped the whole of Patterson's final round.

race_state_note: Alex Baker retains the Wooden Spoon, but a ghastly final round from David Mullin narrowed the gap from 14 to 11 shots — the tightest it has been all week.
